bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /tokenTransfer/:token handler treats knowledge of a random transfer UUID as sufficient authority. POST stores the originating author's token and createdAt under that UUID, but GET neither checks createdAt nor removes the record, so a leaked URL remains redeemable indefinitely and repeatedly. GET also serializes the stored record, including the raw author token, in its response body, defeating the HttpOnly boundary and enabling persistent authorship impersonation. The attacker needs a legitimate user to create a transfer and must obtain its UUID out of band, but needs no Etherpad authentication to redeem it.
flaw_origin: The released introduction 41cb6803d2ac71cadf42f4aa88f37c85275a3879 is a squash of PR #7228. Reconstructing the PR head 399b84d4d148c715322f5fb2eae75a7ba448996c shows that member commit 35519176db4bf6ed0e09d24cc1de58f85552cc24 is the smallest real BIC: it registers the expressCreateServer hook, creates the UUID-backed DB record with createdAt, adds the unauthenticated GET, leaves the record persistent, and returns the complete stored token record. Later PR members only add the createdAt TypeScript field and cookie delivery; they do not originate the no-TTL, replay, or cleartext-body defects.
ai_marker: Absent. The raw commit object for 35519176db4bf6ed0e09d24cc1de58f85552cc24 names author and committer SamTV12345 <40429738+samtv12345@users.noreply.github.com>, has subject 'chore: finished index page', and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/ether/etherpad/security/advisories/GHSA-vqfp-p66c-xrp9 describes the unauthenticated redemption, absent expiration and deletion, raw-token response, affected range >=2.6.0 <=3.0.0, patched range >=3.1.0, released introducer 41cb6803d2ac71cadf42f4aa88f37c85275a3879, and released fix 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996.

Resolve the original PR with `git ls-remote https://github.com/ether/etherpad.git refs/pull/7228/head` (head 399b84d4d148c715322f5fb2eae75a7ba448996c), then run `git log --reverse --format='%H %P %s' b78a803e7aeb4cf46a211ed7dcef10a7887ac3dc..399b84d4d148c715322f5fb2eae75a7ba448996c`. The six members are 409b43f7..., 35519176..., 5517afb3..., 1355d638..., bfb3f70f..., and 399b84d4.... `git show 35519176db4bf6ed0e09d24cc1de58f85552cc24 -- src/ep.json src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts src/static/js/welcome.ts` shows the hook registration plus the first complete POST/GET flow: POST writes `{token,prefsHttp,createdAt}` to `tokenTransfer::<uuid>` and GET fetches and sends that record without expiry or removal.

Origin cross-checks: `git log --reverse -S'res.send(token' --format='%H %s' b78a803e7aeb4cf46a211ed7dcef10a7887ac3dc..399b84d4d148c715322f5fb2eae75a7ba448996c -- src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts` returns only 35519176db4bf6ed0e09d24cc1de58f85552cc24. `git log -L 26,40:src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts 399b84d4d148c715322f5fb2eae75a7ba448996c` traces the GET lookup back to that same member. `git rev-parse 399b84d4d148c715322f5fb2eae75a7ba448996c:src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts 41cb6803d2ac71cadf42f4aa88f37c85275a3879:src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts` prints the identical blob 9a6bb25f18164ef471c351f50ca2f6e8b2d95601 twice, linking the reconstructed PR to the released squash.

Direct parent verification: `git show 409b43f7f4aa9ba4107fc2b329d55f8a05bfcebe:src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts` contains only an expressPreSession POST stub that assigns `req.body.token`; it has no DB import or write, UUID, createdAt, GET route, response containing a token, or redeemable transfer record. Therefore the vulnerable mechanism is absent in the immediate parent.

Pre-fix and fix verification: `git show b96e262782e1ed72999c42cb47fb9140e58fe544:src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts` shows createdAt stored but unchecked, no `db.remove`, and `res.send(tokenData)`. `git show 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 -- src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts` adds a five-minute TRANSFER_TTL_MS check, removes the DB key before responding, rejects missing/non-numeric legacy timestamps, and replaces the body with `{ok: true, prefsHttp}`.

The released fix is also a squash. `git ls-remote https://github.com/ether/etherpad.git refs/pull/7784/head` resolves 29fd3b3638f60342da34bcf4a3bd2c8c269e7e1b; `git log --reverse --format='%H %P %s' b96e262782e1ed72999c42cb47fb9140e58fe544..29fd3b3638f60342da34bcf4a3bd2c8c269e7e1b` identifies a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28 as the direct member containing the tokenTransfer fix. `git rev-parse a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28:src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996:src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts` prints identical blob 175e328a17093517d9f4d02fa7c5c26abff245f6 twice.

Release boundary: `git tag --contains 41cb6803d2ac71cadf42f4aa88f37c85275a3879 --sort=version:refname` starts at 2.6.0, while `git cat-file -e 2.5.3:src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts` reports that the path is absent. `git tag --contains 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 --sort=version:refname` starts at 3.1.0 and excludes 3.0.0. `git show 2.6.0:src/package.json`, `git show 3.0.0:src/package.json`, and `git show 3.1.0:src/package.json` report versions 2.6.0, 3.0.0, and 3.1.0 respectively.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file commit 35519176db4bf6ed0e09d24cc1de58f85552cc24` shows tree b2f1c017931fdca1b3e5efa0251eee55792ca651, parent 409b43f7f4aa9ba4107fc2b329d55f8a05bfcebe, human-named author and committer SamTV12345, and only the subject `chore: finished index page`; there are no trailers or AI/bot markers. AI signals or credits in the later advisory and fix are not evidence about the BIC and were excluded from the verdict.

Lifecycle preservation: `git log --reverse -p 41cb6803d2ac71cadf42f4aa88f37c85275a3879^..8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 -- src/node/hooks/express/tokenTransfer.ts` shows 474918a8814dc93df960c86eae07dfa4df3a5ec8 only adding configurable cookie prefixes and 49bc33f01980564d9ca5f4e45d053be80d175365 moving POST token acquisition to the server-side cookie and making the destination cookie HttpOnly; the latter still ends GET with `res.send(tokenData)` and adds neither expiry enforcement nor deletion. Thus the three audited flaws persist through 3.0.0 until the closing fix.
reasoning: The first complete vulnerable handler is not the public squash landing but the recoverable PR member 35519176db4bf6ed0e09d24cc1de58f85552cc24. Its immediate parent lacks every operative part of the transfer mechanism, while its own diff introduces persistent UUID records and a GET that discloses them. Later changes harden cookie acquisition/delivery but preserve the same replay, lifetime, and response-body defects. The direct fix member a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28 closes all three defects and lands byte-identically for this file in 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996, first released in 3.1.0. Because the BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no permitted AI marker, the causal verdict is NOT_AI; AI involvement in reporting or fixing is out of scope.
